key_insight: CVD-grown single-crystalline cubic D0₃-Fe₃Ge nanoplates exhibit a robust anomalous Hall effect linked to intrinsic Berry curvature and enhanced by epitaxial strain.
engineering_relevance: These nanoplates offer a promising platform for spintronic devices requiring ferromagnetism and anomalous Hall response above room temperature.
method: Grow epitaxial cubic D0₃-Fe₃Ge nanoplates by chemical vapor deposition.
Characterize crystal structure, interfacial strain, magnetism, and Hall transport.
Use DFT to relate strain-induced band reconstruction to anomalous Hall conductivity.
evidence_signal: Structural analysis finds approximately 4.16% interfacial compressive strain, transport scaling supports an intrinsic AHE mechanism, and DFT predicts strain-enhanced conductivity roughly twice the unstrained value.
watch_item: The proposed strain-induced breaking of inversion symmetry remains tentative, and device integration must account for strain relaxation toward the surface.
paper_title: Robust Anomalous Hall Effect in Epitaxial Cubic D0$_3$-Fe$_3$Ge Nanoplates Grown by Chemical Vapor Deposition
